task.title: natural_list takes a conjunction parameter to join with or
task.body:
Why: https://github.com/python-humanize/humanize/issues/214 ; src/humanize/lists.py natural_list always joins with 'and', so a list of alternatives cannot be written as '1, 2 or 3'.
Outcome: `humanize.natural_list(items, conjunction=True)` takes a new keyword parameter `conjunction` (a bool, default True). With `conjunction=False` the last item is joined with 'or' instead of 'and': `natural_list([1, 2, 3], conjunction=False) == '1, 2 or 3'`, `natural_list(["one", "two"], conjunction=False) == 'one or two'`. One item and the empty list are unchanged by the parameter: `natural_list(["one"], conjunction=False) == 'one'`, `natural_list([], conjunction=False) == ''`. Default calls are unchanged: `natural_list([1, 2, 3]) == '1, 2 and 3'`, `natural_list(["one", "two"]) == 'one and two'`, `natural_list(iter(["a", "b", "c"]), conjunction=True) == 'a, b and c'`.
Proof: add tests to tests/test_lists.py.

spec: `humanize.natural_list(items, conjunction=True)` takes a new keyword parameter `conjunction` (a bool, default True). With `conjunction=False` the last item is joined with 'or' instead of 'and': `natural_list([1, 2, 3], conjunction=False) == '1, 2 or 3'`, `natural_list(["one", "two"], conjunction=False) == 'one or two'`. One item and the empty list are unchanged by the parameter: `natural_list(["one"], conjunction=False) == 'one'`, `natural_list([], conjunction=False) == ''`. Default calls are unchanged: `natural_list([1, 2, 3]) == '1, 2 and 3'`, `natural_list(["one", "two"]) == 'one and two'`, `natural_list(iter(["a", "b", "c"]), conjunction=True) == 'a, b and c'`.
install: python3 -m venv .venv && .venv/bin/python -m pip install -q babel -e '.[tests]' && .venv/bin/pybabel --quiet compile --directory src/humanize/locale --domain humanize
